observations.outcome: The study reports approximately 10- to 100-fold lower average Cas9-independent off-target DNA editing for its engineered CBE suite; the reviewed full text states a 69-fold lower ssDNA kcat/Km for YE1 than APOBEC1 in vitro, 1.7- to 4.4-fold differences among named variants in a human-cell ssDNA assay, and roughly 50-90% of BE4max average on-target activity retained in the tested comparisons.

observations.outcome: Corrected fibroblasts showed restored COL7A1 mRNA and type VII collagen protein (western blots stated as n = 1 biological replicate); 3D skin equivalents matured for 20 days showed collagen VII deposition at the dermal-epidermal junction, with C7 intensity significantly increased versus untreated equivalents and not significantly different from wild-type equivalents.

observations.outcome: Treated fibroblasts showed 0.5% of COL7A1 transcripts carrying the c.5047 mutation versus 36% without treatment (the source attributes the untreated sub-50% value to nonsense-mediated decay), and transcriptome-wide RNA sequencing showed no significant increase in A-to-I changes, with 443 differentially expressed genes and no cancer- or metabolic-pathway discrepancies.

observations.outcome: In the engineered Kcnj13W53X/+ΔR mouse, normalized ERG c-wave amplitudes were indistinguishable between targeted- and nontargeting-guide eyes at week 2 (0.9 ± 0.2 versus 0.8 ± 0.1, P = 0.9), while at week 10 the targeted-guide eyes showed 1.6 ± 0.1 versus 0.7 ± 0.1 (P = 0.01), an about-55% amplitude increase; OCT showed preserved retinal structure and multifocal ERG waveforms were localized near injection sites.

observations.outcome: In one mouse-embryo GOTI comparison using the same Tyr-targeting guide (n ≥ 3 embryos per group, non-edited blastomere of the same embryo as reference), ABE8e-edited cells averaged 371 genome-wide SNVs per embryo versus 13 in Cre controls, with 94% A-to-G/T-to-C conversions at TA contexts and no shared off-target sites between embryos; replication with three further guides averaged 279, 343 and 387 SNVs per embryo (21- to 30-fold over controls).

The abstract rounds the 371-versus-13 comparison to approximately 30-fold while the Results state more than 28-fold; both are retained as source statistics.

observations.outcome: In the hereditary tyrosinemia type I mouse model, an initial medication-maintained cohort showed comparable average on-target editing for ABE8e-Y149V and ABE8e (35.8% versus 35.5%) with lower bystander and indel outcomes for Y149V; after medication withdrawal, saline-injected controls lost an average 20% of body weight by day 32 and were euthanized while Y149V-treated mice gained weight normally and were phenotypically indistinguishable from wild type; day-30 liver sequencing averaged 69.0% target editing with negligible bystander edits or indels, and serum AST, ALT and bilirubin were restored to levels comparable with reference groups.

Liver allele fractions can reflect selective survival of edited hepatocytes and do not equal initial cell coverage, and animal counts per group are not stated in the accessed text. This is a short-term disease model, not ordinary-aging repair.

observations.outcome: Small-molecule-controllable split-engineered base editors were reported to reduce cellular toxicity and enable inducible in vivo functional-genomics screens, with guide libraries of about 11,000 in vitro and about 3,700 in vivo, and an Adar1 tiling screen identifying critical residues that elicit non-cell-autonomous cancer dependencies in vivo.

observations.outcome: In preclinical in-vivo models with explicit group sizes (Nalm6 leukemia: 18 E81K-edited versus 19 control and 3 untransduced mice; Sh-Sy5y solid tumor: 11/11/4; neuroblastoma B7H3-28z: 9/9/4; T cells from 2-4 healthy donors per experiment with TRBC co-knockout), the activating PIK3CD E81K substitution enhanced proliferation, metabolic fitness, effector function and long-term functional persistence of 4-1BBz CAR T cells with improved survival, while the attenuating L32P substitution improved memory formation and function of 28z CAR T cells.

observations.limits: These are preclinical engineered-cell potency findings in small immunodeficient-xenograft groups. Base editing deliberately reprograms a signaling allele; it does not correct a tumor-driver mutation, and no human dosing, safety or clinical protocol follows from this row.

observations.outcome: In the Nalm6 leukemia NSG mouse model, E81K-edited TRBC-knockout 19BBz CAR T cells (n = 18 mice) showed enhanced tumor control with long-term remissions and significantly improved survival versus control 19BBz CAR T cells (n = 19) and untransduced T cells (n = 3), using T cells from four unrelated healthy donors and a source Mantel-Cox test; a rechallenge experiment (n = 4 mice per group) showed functional persistence.

observations.outcome: The source's safety analyses of E81K-edited 19BBz CAR T cells found no signs of lymphomagenesis or increased side effects: no aberrant antigen-independent growth in long-term culture, no morbidity or weight changes over 150 days (n = 19 per group), 66-day necropsies with intact organ structures and tissue T-cell counts (n = 4 per group), unaffected liver enzymes (n = 4) and no cytokine-release-syndrome-associated serum signatures (n = 5).

observations.outcome: Detectable clonal blood somatic mutations were rare under 40 years of age and rose with age: 9.5% (219 of 2,300 persons) at 70-79, 11.7% (37 of 317) at 80-89 and 18.4% (19 of 103) at 90-108 years, with most variants in DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1.

observations.outcome: No off-target mutations above background were found in the source's testing of ABE-edited macaque livers: CIRCLE-seq-, CHANGE-seq- and iGUIDE-nominated top candidate off-target sites showed no substantial A-to-G editing, and mouse clonal whole-genome sequencing showed no increased A-to-G burden or TadA signature.

observations.limits: A no-detected-off-target result in the source's candidate-site and clonal genomic-DNA testing is not whole-genome absence across every condition or long-term safety. Absence of a detected signal is not zero risk.

observations.outcome: Re-dosing at a 2-week interval did not increase editing in macaques (3.31 ± 1.73% and 24.14 ± 1.52% after repeat dosing versus 2.03 ± 0.85% and 27.6 ± 5.87% after single dosing at the two dose levels), and SpCas9- and TadA-specific IgG were detected at Day 29 in both repeat-dose groups; in high-dose animals the full text states PCSK9 reductions of 26% (single) and 39% (repeat) and LDL reductions of 9% and 19% from baseline, while the accessed abstract states 32% and 14%.

observations.follow_up: Day-22 and Day-29 serum timepoints relative to Day -12 and Day -1 baselines; Day-29 necropsy
observations.limits: An absent editing increase after repeat dosing and a detected humoral immune response in macaques are repeat-dosing durability caveats, not human immunogenicity estimates or dosing protocols. The abstract-level 32%/14% and Results-level per-group biomarker percentages differ in aggregation and are both retained as source statistics without reconciliation.

observations.outcome: On-target editing was measured in nine organs of high-dose macaques: below 1% in eight examined organs, and 6.1 ± 2.7% (single-dose) and 12.4 ± 7.8% (repeat-dose) in spleen.

observations.outcome: Second- and third-generation cytidine base editors achieved permanent correction of about 15-75% of total cellular DNA across four transformed human and murine cell lines with indels typically at or below 1% (below 0.1% for the second generation); in disease-model settings, an APOE4-mimic astrocyte locus exceeded 50% correction (4.6-6.1% indels) and a TP53 Tyr163Cys cancer-line locus reached 3.3-7.6% correction (at most 0.7% indels), versus far lower correction and far higher indels in the Cas9-plus-donor comparisons.

observations.outcome: Seventh-generation adenine base editors converted target A•T to G•C at about 50% average efficiency in human cells (abstract) with product purity typically at or above 99.9% and indels typically at or below 0.1%; the evolution ladder reports six-locus averages of 11±2.9%, 14±2.4% and 29±2.6% (mean±SD of three biological replicates) with a stated YAC sequence-context preference, and the HDR comparison reports 10-35% (48 h) and 55-68% (120 h) target-mutation frequencies.

observations.limits: Target- and context-dependent cell-culture statistics; the GUIDE-seq-anchored off-target comparison (9 of 12 loci modified by Cas9 versus 4 of 12 by ABE variants at lower levels) rests on the source's stated assumption, and no comprehensive ABE off-target profiling method existed at the time.

observations.outcome: Prime editing (a Cas9 H840A nickase fused to an engineered reverse transcriptase, programmed by a prime-editing guide RNA) installed more than 175 edits in human cells including all 12 point-mutation types and targeted insertions and deletions; the PE2 pentamutant improved point-mutation efficiency 1.6- to 5.1-fold over PE1; disease-model corrections included HBB (sickle cell), HEXA (Tay-Sachs) and PRNP edits in human cells.

observations.limits: A cell-level capability survey in four human cell lines and primary mouse cortical neurons; off-target comparisons are at known Cas9 off-target sites, not genome-wide profiling, and the up-to-89%-correctable figure is a computed estimate.
